newNodes.name: Wayfinding lore
newNodes.emerged: ~40 kya inferred from raw materials carried hundreds of km; ethnographic route songs (songlines)
newNodes.prereqRationale: oral_tradition: routes, landmarks and water sources are memorised and passed on in song and story.
newNodes.rationale: oral_tradition: routes, landmarks and water sources are memorised and passed on in song and story.
newNodes.desc: Bands memorise routes, landmarks, water holes and star rises in song and story, so a party can travel far beyond its home range and find its way back.
newNodes.effectRationale: Remembered routes let explorers range further from home and return.
newNodes.distinctFrom: oral_tradition carries any story; this is the practical knowledge of routes used for travel.

newNodes.name: Guest right
newNodes.emerged: ~40 kya inferred from shell beads exchanged across band territories; universal in recorded foragers
newNodes.prereqRationale: gift_exchange: visits to exchange partners require that strangers who come in peace are fed and protected.
newNodes.rationale: gift_exchange: visits to exchange partners require that strangers who come in peace are fed and protected.
newNodes.desc: Strangers who come in peace are fed and protected for a time, so people can cross other bands' land to trade, marry or resettle without being treated as raiders.
newNodes.effectRationale: Safe passage through others' land lets migrants travel further.
newNodes.distinctFrom: gift_exchange moves goods between partners; guest right protects the person travelling.

newNodes.name: Village defences
newNodes.emerged: ~8,000 BCE wall and tower at Jericho; ~5,000 BCE ditched and palisaded villages in central Europe
newNodes.prereqRationale: war_band: the defenders are the community's armed men. stone_dry OR timber_frame: walls of stone or palisades of timber.
newNodes.rationale: war_band: the defenders are the community's armed men. stone_dry OR timber_frame: walls of stone or palisades of timber.
newNodes.desc: The village digs ditches, raises a wall or palisade and keeps a watch, so raiders cannot simply carry off the stored harvest.
newNodes.effectRationale: Defended stores survive raids and are there to relieve hunger.
newNodes.distinctFrom: war_band raids others; defences protect the community's own stores.

newNodes.name: Warrior retinues
newNodes.emerged: ~4,500 BCE weapon-rich graves at Varna; ~2,800 BCE Corded Ware battle-axe burials
newNodes.prereqRationale: hereditary_rank: a ranked leader keeps the retinue. war_band: the retinue is a permanent war band.
newNodes.rationale: hereditary_rank: a ranked leader keeps the retinue. war_band: the retinue is a permanent war band.
newNodes.desc: A chief keeps armed followers who are fed from his hall and fight at his call, and who also collect what is owed to him.
newNodes.effectRationale: Armed followers enforce tribute and dues.
newNodes.distinctFrom: war_band forms for one raid; a retinue is kept all year by one leader.

newNodes.name: Daughter villages
newNodes.emerged: ~7,000 BCE farming villages spread into Greece; ~5,500 BCE Linearbandkeramik spread across central Europe
newNodes.prereqRationale: cereal_cultivation: farmers carry seed to new land. kin_council: the household heads decide who goes.
newNodes.rationale: cereal_cultivation: farmers carry seed to new land. kin_council: the household heads decide who goes.
newNodes.desc: When a village grows too large, a group of households leaves with seed and stock to found a new village nearby.
newNodes.effectRationale: Organised fission sends larger founding parties.
newNodes.distinctFrom: daughter_colonies (A4) are overseas cities; this is overland village fission among farmers.

newNodes.name: Island colonization voyages
newNodes.emerged: ~8,500 BCE farmers reach Cyprus with goats, pigs and cattle; ~7,000 BCE Crete settled
newNodes.prereqRationale: raft OR dugout: open-water craft. sheep_goat: settlers carry breeding stock to found herds on the island.
newNodes.rationale: raft OR dugout: open-water craft. sheep_goat: settlers carry breeding stock to found herds on the island.
newNodes.desc: Settlers sail to islands with seed, breeding stock and supplies to found new communities beyond sight of land.
newNodes.effectRationale: Planned sea crossings carry explorers further per expedition.
newNodes.distinctFrom: wayfinding_lore is route memory on land; this is planned settlement across open water.

newNodes.name: Exchange partners
newNodes.emerged: ~7,000 BCE Anatolian obsidian in the Levant; ~5,000 BCE Alpine jadeite axes and Spondylus shell across Europe
newNodes.prereqRationale: gift_exchange: the goods moved. communal_feasts: partnerships are renewed at feasts between communities.
newNodes.rationale: gift_exchange: the goods moved. communal_feasts: partnerships are renewed at feasts between communities.
newNodes.desc: Communities keep standing exchange partners in other villages and renew the tie at feasts, so axes, shell and stone pass from hand to hand across hundreds of km.
newNodes.effectRationale: Standing partnerships move goods toward the communities that lack them.

civ7.analog: Code of Laws (Improve Trade Relations action)

newNodes.rationale: appointed_officials: officials stock and issue rations. donkey OR cart: pack and draught transport move the stores.

newNodes.prereqRationale: appointed_officials: the crown appoints and supplies the leader. sail_square OR donkey: by sea or by caravan.
newNodes.rationale: appointed_officials: the crown appoints and supplies the leader. sail_square OR donkey: by sea or by caravan.
newNodes.desc: The crown sends organised expeditions to distant lands for incense, gold and stone, and records what they find.
newNodes.effectRationale: State-supplied expeditions reach lands beyond the usual range.
newNodes.distinctFrom: royal_envoys go to known courts; expeditions go to lands not yet known.

newNodes.name: Frontier fortresses
newNodes.emerged: ~1,860 BCE Middle Kingdom forts at the Second Cataract; ~1,800 BCE Semna despatches
newNodes.prereqRationale: territorial_kingship: a kingdom with a frontier to hold. appointed_officials: commandants and scribes man the forts.
newNodes.rationale: territorial_kingship: a kingdom with a frontier to hold. appointed_officials: commandants and scribes man the forts.
newNodes.desc: A chain of forts with commandants and scribes holds a frontier, controls crossings and reports movements to the capital.
newNodes.effectRationale: Garrisoned forts project the kingdom's authority to its edge.
newNodes.distinctFrom: service_tenure settles soldiers on land; fortresses are state garrisons at the border.

newNodes.name: Siege and road engineers
newNodes.emerged: ~865 BCE Assyrian sappers, ramps and river crossings in Ashurnasirpal II's reliefs
newNodes.prereqRationale: standing_army: engineers are permanent specialists. siege_ram: the siege train they build and move.
newNodes.rationale: standing_army: engineers are permanent specialists. siege_ram: the siege train they build and move.
newNodes.desc: Specialist troops build ramps, bridges and tracks for the army, and their skills are turned to roads in peace.
newNodes.effectRationale: Trained engineers build more path per worker.
newNodes.distinctFrom: siege_ram is the machine; this is the corps that builds and moves armies.

newNodes.name: State resettlement
newNodes.emerged: ~745 BCE Tiglath-Pileser III resettles conquered peoples; ~587 BCE Babylonian exile
newNodes.prereqRationale: provincial_administration: governors receive and settle the newcomers. standing_army: the army moves them.
newNodes.rationale: provincial_administration: governors receive and settle the newcomers. standing_army: the army moves them.
newNodes.desc: The state moves whole communities from conquered lands to new provinces to farm empty land and break old loyalties.
newNodes.effectRationale: State-organised moves carry people over very long distances.
newNodes.distinctFrom: daughter_colonies send volunteers out; resettlement moves whole communities by order.

newNodes.name: Veteran colonies
newNodes.emerged: ~300 BCE Ptolemaic cleruchs in the Fayum; ~100 BCE Roman colonies of discharged legionaries
newNodes.prereqRationale: standing_army: long-service soldiers to discharge. land_registry: surveyed plots to grant them.
newNodes.rationale: standing_army: long-service soldiers to discharge. land_registry: surveyed plots to grant them.
newNodes.desc: Discharged soldiers receive surveyed plots in new or conquered land, founding colonies loyal to the state.
newNodes.effectRationale: Veteran settlers form large founding parties and bring marginal land into use.
newNodes.distinctFrom: daughter_colonies are civic foundations; these are state grants to discharged soldiers.

newNodes.name: Military roads
newNodes.emerged: 312 BCE Via Appia built for the Samnite wars; 212 BCE Qin Straight Road
newNodes.prereqRationale: standing_army: the army builds and uses the road. road_paved: the paving technique.
newNodes.rationale: standing_army: the army builds and uses the road. road_paved: the paving technique.
newNodes.desc: The state builds straight, paved, all-weather roads to move armies fast; merchants and couriers use them too.
newNodes.effectRationale: All-weather trunk roads raise overland travel speed.
newNodes.distinctFrom: road_paved is the technique; this is the state road network and its upkeep.

newNodes.name: Hegemonic leagues
newNodes.emerged: ~478 BCE Delian League; ~338 BCE League of Corinth
newNodes.prereqRationale: sworn_treaties: the league is sworn. citizen_assembly OR elite_council: member cities decide through their councils.
newNodes.rationale: sworn_treaties: the league is sworn. citizen_assembly OR elite_council: member cities decide through their councils.
newNodes.desc: Allied cities swear to a common league led by the strongest, paying into a shared treasury for a common fleet or army.
newNodes.effectRationale: League contributions are collected from allies on a fixed assessment.
newNodes.distinctFrom: oath_alliance binds equals; a league has a leader, a treasury and assessed dues.

newNodes.name: Military treatises
newNodes.emerged: ~500 BCE Sunzi's Art of War; ~350 BCE Aeneas Tacticus
newNodes.prereqRationale: standing_army: a profession to teach. philosophical_schools: systematic written argument.
newNodes.rationale: standing_army: a profession to teach. philosophical_schools: systematic written argument.
newNodes.desc: Commanders write down doctrine on scouting, spies, supply and terrain, and officers study it.
newNodes.effectRationale: Doctrine on scouts and spies lets formations see further.
newNodes.distinctFrom: military_academies (A7) are schools; this is written doctrine itself.

newNodes.name: Slave-soldier corps
newNodes.emerged: ~833 CE al-Mu'tasim's Turkic ghulam guard; ~1,380 CE Ottoman Janissaries
newNodes.prereqRationale: standing_army: a permanent force. coined_wage: the soldiers draw cash pay and stipends.
newNodes.rationale: standing_army: a permanent force. coined_wage: the soldiers draw cash pay and stipends.
newNodes.desc: The ruler buys or levies boys from outside, trains them as soldiers, and promotes the able to command and governorships.
newNodes.effectRationale: Outsiders rise by service into command and office.
newNodes.distinctFrom: military_rule is a regime; this is a recruitment and promotion system.

newNodes.name: Safe-conduct
newNodes.emerged: ~650 CE aman granted to foreign envoys and merchants; ~1,414 CE English Safe Conducts Act
newNodes.prereqRationale: royal_envoys: envoys are the first holders of safe-conduct. law_code: the guarantee is enforceable law.
newNodes.rationale: royal_envoys: envoys are the first holders of safe-conduct. law_code: the guarantee is enforceable law.
newNodes.desc: A ruler's written guarantee protects named foreigners, their goods and their servants while they travel in his land.
newNodes.effectRationale: Guaranteed safety lets travellers and migrants go further.
newNodes.distinctFrom: guest_right is custom among bands; safe-conduct is a written state guarantee.

newNodes.name: Merchant consuls
newNodes.emerged: ~1,100 CE Genoese and Venetian consuls in Levantine ports; ~1,268 CE Venetian bailo at Constantinople
newNodes.prereqRationale: trade_treaties: the consul enforces treaty terms. commercial_law: he judges merchants' disputes.
newNodes.rationale: trade_treaties: the consul enforces treaty terms. commercial_law: he judges merchants' disputes.
newNodes.desc: Merchants abroad elect or receive a consul who judges their disputes, speaks for them to the ruler and keeps their warehouse.
newNodes.effectRationale: Protected warehouses and quick justice cut the cost of foreign trade.
newNodes.distinctFrom: trade_treaties are agreements; consuls are officers resident abroad who enforce them.

newNodes.name: Settlement charters
newNodes.emerged: ~974 CE carta puebla of Castrojeriz; ~1,150 CE locators settle villages east of the Elbe
newNodes.prereqRationale: land_registry: plots are measured. municipal_charter: settlers receive a written charter of rights.
newNodes.rationale: land_registry: plots are measured. municipal_charter: settlers receive a written charter of rights.
newNodes.desc: Lords grant written charters with free plots, low dues and self-government to attract settlers to frontier land.
newNodes.effectRationale: Better terms draw migrants to new land and swell founding parties.
newNodes.distinctFrom: municipal_charter governs a town; settlement charters recruit settlers to empty land.

newNodes.name: Marcher lordships
newNodes.emerged: ~795 CE Carolingian Spanish March; ~1,070 CE Welsh Marches
newNodes.prereqRationale: service_tenure: march lords hold land for war service. provincial_administration: the march is a frontier province.
newNodes.rationale: service_tenure: march lords hold land for war service. provincial_administration: the march is a frontier province.
newNodes.desc: Frontier districts are granted to lords with wide powers to raise troops, build castles and push the border outward.
newNodes.effectRationale: Empowered frontier lords hold distant border land.
newNodes.distinctFrom: frontier_fortresses are royal garrisons; marches delegate the frontier to lords.

newNodes.name: Army magazines
newNodes.emerged: ~1,670 CE Louvois's magazine system; ~1,771 CE Prussian magazines opened for famine relief
newNodes.prereqRationale: standing_army: the army the magazines feed. public_granaries: state grain storage practice.
newNodes.rationale: standing_army: the army the magazines feed. public_granaries: state grain storage practice.
newNodes.desc: The state keeps grain magazines for the army along the frontier and opens them to the public in famine years.
newNodes.effectRationale: Military grain reserves are released to relieve famine.
newNodes.distinctFrom: public_granaries are civil stores; magazines are military stores also used in famine.

newNodes.name: Corps of engineers
newNodes.emerged: ~1,690 CE Vauban's corps of engineers; ~1,716 CE French Corps des ponts et chaussées
newNodes.prereqRationale: standing_army: a permanent corps. trace_italienne: engineers are trained for bastion fortification.
newNodes.rationale: standing_army: a permanent corps. trace_italienne: engineers are trained for bastion fortification.
newNodes.desc: A permanent corps of trained engineers designs fortresses, bridges and roads and surveys the ground.
newNodes.effectRationale: Surveyed, engineered routes cost less to build.
newNodes.distinctFrom: siege_engineers are field troops; this is a trained professional corps.

newNodes.name: Chartered companies
newNodes.emerged: 1600 CE English East India Company; 1602 CE Dutch East India Company
newNodes.prereqRationale: joint_stock: the company is a joint-stock body. state_exploration: the charter grants the routes found by state voyages.
newNodes.rationale: joint_stock: the company is a joint-stock body. state_exploration: the charter grants the routes found by state voyages.
newNodes.desc: The state charters a company with a trade monopoly and powers to fortify, make treaties and govern overseas.
newNodes.effectRationale: Company sales bring overseas cargoes to home markets regularly.
newNodes.distinctFrom: joint_stock is the firm form; this is a firm granted sovereign powers overseas.

newNodes.name: Military railways
newNodes.emerged: ~1,859 CE French troops sent by rail to Italy; ~1,866 CE Prussian railway mobilization
newNodes.prereqRationale: general_staff: staff timetables plan the moves. railway: the network used.
newNodes.rationale: general_staff: staff timetables plan the moves. railway: the network used.
newNodes.desc: The staff plans railway timetables to move troops and supplies, and lines are built where the army needs them.
newNodes.effectRationale: Planned rail movement speeds overland travel.
newNodes.distinctFrom: railway is the technology; this is its planned military use.

newNodes.name: Trained reserves
newNodes.emerged: ~1,813 CE Prussian Landwehr; ~1,867 CE Austro-Hungarian reserve system
newNodes.prereqRationale: universal_conscription: reserves are former conscripts after short active service.
newNodes.rationale: universal_conscription: reserves are former conscripts after short active service.
newNodes.desc: Conscripts serve a short term, then return home as trained reserves called up only in war.
newNodes.effectRationale: Short service returns young men to the farms in their working prime.
newNodes.distinctFrom: universal_conscription calls men up; reserves send them home trained.

newNodes.name: Colonial regiments
newNodes.emerged: ~1,757 CE East India Company sepoy battalions; ~1,857 CE Tirailleurs sénégalais
newNodes.prereqRationale: colonial_administration: the colony raises the troops. mercenary_contracts: soldiers serve for pay under contract.
newNodes.rationale: colonial_administration: the colony raises the troops. mercenary_contracts: soldiers serve for pay under contract.
newNodes.desc: The colonial government raises regiments from local recruits under contract to garrison and police its territories.
newNodes.effectRationale: Locally raised garrisons hold distant territory.
newNodes.distinctFrom: mercenary_contracts hire foreign soldiers; these are standing colonial units.

newNodes.name: Consular service
newNodes.emerged: ~1,825 CE British Consular Act; ~1,856 CE US consular reform
newNodes.prereqRationale: merchant_consuls: the older office. resident_embassies: consuls join a state's foreign service.
newNodes.rationale: merchant_consuls: the older office. resident_embassies: consuls join a state's foreign service.
newNodes.desc: Salaried state consuls in foreign ports protect nationals and report on markets, prices and shipping.
newNodes.effectRationale: Regular market reports let traders close price gaps faster.
newNodes.distinctFrom: merchant_consuls serve one merchant community; this is a state service reporting on markets.

newNodes.name: River commissions
newNodes.emerged: ~1,815 CE Central Commission for Navigation on the Rhine; ~1,856 CE European Danube Commission
newNodes.prereqRationale: great_power_congress: the Rhine commission was created at Vienna and the Danube one at Paris.
newNodes.rationale: great_power_congress: the Rhine commission was created at Vienna and the Danube one at Paris.
newNodes.desc: States along a river set common rules, tolls and channel works under a standing commission so ships move freely.
newNodes.effectRationale: Free navigation and dredged channels cut river haulage costs.
newNodes.distinctFrom: international_organizations are general bodies; this regulates one shared river.

newNodes.name: Coaling stations
newNodes.emerged: ~1,839 CE Aden taken as a coaling port; ~1,898 CE Pacific coaling bases
newNodes.prereq: state_navy AND (steamboat OR screw_propeller) AND colonial_administration
newNodes.prereqRationale: state_navy: the fleet that needs coal. steamboat OR screw_propeller: steam ships. colonial_administration: the ports are held as colonies.
newNodes.rationale: state_navy: the fleet that needs coal. steamboat OR screw_propeller: steam ships. colonial_administration: the ports are held as colonies.
newNodes.desc: The navy holds a chain of ports stocked with coal so steam ships can cross oceans.
newNodes.effectRationale: Refuelling ports let steam expeditions go further per voyage.
newNodes.distinctFrom: state_navy is the fleet; this is its global base network.

newNodes.name: Geographical societies
newNodes.emerged: ~1,821 CE Société de Géographie; ~1,830 CE Royal Geographical Society
newNodes.prereqRationale: scientific_societies: learned-society form. state_exploration: voyages they fund and publish.
newNodes.rationale: scientific_societies: learned-society form. state_exploration: voyages they fund and publish.
newNodes.desc: Learned societies fund expeditions, publish maps and train explorers in survey.
newNodes.effectRationale: Funded, surveyed expeditions reach further.
newNodes.distinctFrom: state_exploration is crown voyages; this is private learned exploration.

newNodes.name: Assisted emigration
newNodes.emerged: ~1,831 CE assisted passages to New South Wales; ~1,840 CE Colonial Land and Emigration Commission
newNodes.prereqRationale: colonial_administration: the colony pays the passages. land_registry: land sales fund them.
newNodes.rationale: colonial_administration: the colony pays the passages. land_registry: land sales fund them.
newNodes.desc: Colonies pay the passage of chosen emigrants from land-sale revenue so labourers can reach distant colonies.
newNodes.effectRationale: Paid passages carry migrants across oceans.
newNodes.distinctFrom: settler_land_grants give land; this pays for the journey.

newNodes.name: Colonial self-government
newNodes.emerged: ~1,848 CE responsible government in Nova Scotia and Canada; ~1,867 CE Canadian Confederation
newNodes.prereqRationale: colonial_administration: the colony. ministerial_responsibility: ministers answer to the colonial assembly.
newNodes.rationale: colonial_administration: the colony. ministerial_responsibility: ministers answer to the colonial assembly.
newNodes.desc: Settler colonies gain their own cabinet answerable to an elected assembly, while foreign affairs stay with the empire.
newNodes.effectRationale: Settlers govern their own affairs, removing a source of revolt.
newNodes.distinctFrom: indirect_rule governs through princes; this hands self-government to settlers.

newNodes.name: Peacekeeping
newNodes.emerged: ~1,948 CE UN truce observers in Palestine; ~1,956 CE UN Emergency Force
newNodes.prereqRationale: collective_security: the operations are mandated by the collective-security body.
newNodes.rationale: collective_security: the operations are mandated by the collective-security body.
newNodes.desc: International forces, accepted by both sides, watch ceasefire lines and protect aid convoys.
newNodes.effectRationale: Protected relief convoys reduce famine deaths in conflict zones.
newNodes.distinctFrom: collective_security pledges action; peacekeeping is a neutral force in the field.

newNodes.name: International food aid
newNodes.emerged: ~1,954 CE US Food for Peace; ~1,961 CE World Food Programme
newNodes.prereqRationale: international_organizations: the programme body. public_granaries: the state food-reserve practice it extends.
newNodes.rationale: international_organizations: the programme body. public_granaries: the state food-reserve practice it extends.
newNodes.desc: Surplus food is shipped through international programmes to countries in famine.
newNodes.effectRationale: Outside stocks relieve famine.
newNodes.distinctFrom: public_granaries are national; this pools food across states.

newNodes.name: Law of the sea
newNodes.emerged: ~1,958 CE Geneva conventions on the sea; ~1,982 CE UN Convention on the Law of the Sea
newNodes.prereqRationale: law_of_nations: the body of law codified. international_organizations: the conferences that agree it.
newNodes.rationale: law_of_nations: the body of law codified. international_organizations: the conferences that agree it.
newNodes.desc: Treaties fix territorial waters and economic zones, giving coastal states rights over fisheries and the seabed.
newNodes.effectRationale: Secure rights to coastal fisheries and seabed raise extractive output.
newNodes.distinctFrom: law_of_nations covers neutrality at sea; this assigns ocean resources.

newNodes.name: Civil aviation agreements
newNodes.emerged: ~1,919 CE Paris Convention on air navigation; ~1,944 CE Chicago Convention
newNodes.prereqRationale: international_organizations: the treaty body (ICAO). aircraft: what is regulated.
newNodes.rationale: international_organizations: the treaty body (ICAO). aircraft: what is regulated.
newNodes.desc: States agree rights to fly over and land in each other's territory and common air safety rules.
newNodes.effectRationale: Scheduled international flights let migrants travel further.
newNodes.distinctFrom: international_organizations is general; this opens airspace.

newNodes.name: Development lending
newNodes.emerged: ~1,944 CE Bretton Woods conference; ~1,947 CE first World Bank loans
newNodes.prereqRationale: international_organizations: the lending body. central_banking: the monetary institutions it works with.
newNodes.rationale: international_organizations: the lending body. central_banking: the monetary institutions it works with.
newNodes.desc: International banks lend to governments for roads, dams and power plants.
newNodes.effectRationale: Long-term loans make road building cheaper to finance.
newNodes.distinctFrom: central_banking is national; this lends across borders for infrastructure.

newNodes.name: Passport-free travel areas
newNodes.emerged: ~1,952 CE Nordic passport union; ~1,985 CE Schengen Agreement
newNodes.prereqRationale: international_organizations: the agreement body. customs_union: removing border checks follows removing tariffs.
newNodes.rationale: international_organizations: the agreement body. customs_union: removing border checks follows removing tariffs.
newNodes.desc: Member states abolish passport checks at their common borders and let citizens live and work across them.
newNodes.effectRationale: Open borders raise the rate of movement.
newNodes.distinctFrom: customs_union frees goods; this frees people.

newNodes.name: Academic exchange
newNodes.emerged: ~1,946 CE Fulbright Program; ~1,987 CE Erasmus Programme
newNodes.prereqRationale: research_university: the institutions exchanging. international_organizations: the programmes.
newNodes.rationale: research_university: the institutions exchanging. international_organizations: the programmes.
newNodes.desc: Governments fund students and scholars to study and teach abroad.
newNodes.effectRationale: Visiting faculty and returning graduates help universities mature faster.
newNodes.distinctFrom: research_university is domestic; this links universities across states.

newNodes.name: International standards bodies
newNodes.emerged: ~1,906 CE International Electrotechnical Commission; ~1,947 CE ISO; ~1,968 CE ISO container standard
newNodes.prereqRationale: international_organizations: the standards body. interchangeable_parts: the practice of standard dimensions.
newNodes.rationale: international_organizations: the standards body. interchangeable_parts: the practice of standard dimensions.
newNodes.desc: States and industries agree common standards for parts, measures and shipping containers.
newNodes.effectRationale: Standard containers and parts cut handling costs.
newNodes.distinctFrom: multilateral_trade_rules govern tariffs; standards govern the goods themselves.

newNodes.name: Shared-river treaties
newNodes.emerged: ~1,929 CE Nile Waters Agreement; ~1,960 CE Indus Waters Treaty
newNodes.prereqRationale: river_commissions: standing river diplomacy. irrigation_canal: the water being allocated.
newNodes.rationale: river_commissions: standing river diplomacy. irrigation_canal: the water being allocated.
newNodes.desc: States sharing a river divide its water by treaty so irrigation works on both sides have an assured supply.
newNodes.effectRationale: Assured irrigation water raises yields.
newNodes.distinctFrom: river_commissions regulate navigation; this allocates water.

newNodes.name: International weather service
newNodes.emerged: ~1,950 CE World Meteorological Organization; ~1,963 CE World Weather Watch
newNodes.prereqRationale: international_organizations: the WMO. weather_prediction: the forecasts shared.
newNodes.rationale: international_organizations: the WMO. weather_prediction: the forecasts shared.
newNodes.desc: States share weather observations in real time so every country can forecast storms, frost and drought.
newNodes.effectRationale: Shared forecasts let farmers time sowing and harvest, steadying yields.
newNodes.distinctFrom: weather_prediction is the science; this is the exchange of observations.

newNodes.name: Intelligence agencies
newNodes.emerged: ~1,909 CE British Secret Service Bureau; ~1,947 CE Central Intelligence Agency
newNodes.prereqRationale: general_staff: the intelligence branch of the staff. radio: signals interception.
newNodes.rationale: general_staff: the intelligence branch of the staff. radio: signals interception.
newNodes.desc: A permanent agency gathers and analyses intelligence from agents, signals and photographs.
newNodes.effectRationale: Formations receive intelligence beyond their own sight.
newNodes.distinctFrom: general_staff plans; this agency collects information.

newNodes.name: Satellite reconnaissance
newNodes.emerged: ~1,960 CE Corona photo-reconnaissance satellites
newNodes.prereqRationale: satellite: the platform. military_intelligence: the agency that runs it.
newNodes.rationale: satellite: the platform. military_intelligence: the agency that runs it.
newNodes.desc: Satellites photograph any part of the earth and return the images.
newNodes.effectRationale: Orbital imagery reveals land beyond the explorer's reach.
newNodes.distinctFrom: military_intelligence uses agents and signals; this uses orbital imagery.

newNodes.name: Motor transport corps
newNodes.emerged: ~1,916 CE lorry convoys on the Voie Sacrée at Verdun; ~1,944 CE Red Ball Express
newNodes.prereqRationale: general_staff: plans the convoys. automobile_mass: mass-produced lorries.
newNodes.rationale: general_staff: plans the convoys. automobile_mass: mass-produced lorries.
newNodes.desc: Army lorry columns carry supplies far beyond the railhead.
newNodes.effectRationale: Lorry columns sustain longer road routes.
newNodes.distinctFrom: military_railways move by rail; this carries supplies by road from the railhead.

newNodes.name: Civil defence
newNodes.emerged: ~1,935 CE British Air Raid Precautions; ~1,950 CE US Federal Civil Defense Administration
newNodes.prereqRationale: total_mobilization: the whole population is organised. aircraft: the air threat.
newNodes.rationale: total_mobilization: the whole population is organised. aircraft: the air threat.
newNodes.desc: Wardens, shelters and emergency food depots protect civilians in war and disaster.
newNodes.effectRationale: Emergency food depots enlarge stores held against disaster.
newNodes.distinctFrom: total_mobilization directs production; civil defence protects civilians.

newNodes.name: Ration books
newNodes.emerged: ~1,917 CE German and British food rationing; ~1,940 CE British ration books
newNodes.prereqRationale: total_mobilization: rationing is part of directing the war economy.
newNodes.rationale: total_mobilization: rationing is part of directing the war economy.
newNodes.desc: Scarce food is shared by fixed rations per person so households get through shortages.
newNodes.effectRationale: Fair shares let households absorb shortfalls.
newNodes.distinctFrom: total_mobilization directs production; rationing divides consumption.

newNodes.name: Veterans' benefits
newNodes.emerged: ~1,944 CE GI Bill; ~1,945 CE British Further Education and Training Scheme
newNodes.prereqRationale: universal_conscription: the veterans. compulsory_education: the school system that admits them.
newNodes.rationale: universal_conscription: the veterans. compulsory_education: the school system that admits them.
newNodes.desc: Former soldiers receive paid schooling, training and home loans.
newNodes.effectRationale: Paid education moves veterans into skilled classes.
newNodes.distinctFrom: universal_conscription calls up; this rewards and retrains after service.

newNodes.name: Counter-insurgency doctrine
newNodes.emerged: ~1,950 CE Briggs Plan in Malaya; ~1,964 CE Galula's Counterinsurgency Warfare
newNodes.prereqRationale: military_intelligence: insurgency is fought with information. colonial_administration: the doctrine came from colonial emergencies.
newNodes.rationale: military_intelligence: insurgency is fought with information. colonial_administration: the doctrine came from colonial emergencies.
newNodes.desc: Armies and police protect the population, gather intelligence and address grievances to isolate insurgents.
newNodes.effectRationale: Unrest disrupts less output where order is restored.
newNodes.distinctFrom: civil_police keep ordinary order; this counters armed insurgency.

newNodes.name: Strategic stockpiles
newNodes.emerged: ~1,939 CE US Strategic Materials Act; ~1,975 CE Strategic Petroleum Reserve
newNodes.prereqRationale: total_mobilization: stockpiles prepare for the next mobilisation.
newNodes.rationale: total_mobilization: stockpiles prepare for the next mobilisation.
newNodes.desc: The state stores fuel, metals and food and releases them to the market when supplies fail.
newNodes.effectRationale: Reserves are released to markets faster in shortages.
newNodes.distinctFrom: civil_defence stocks food locally; this holds national strategic reserves.

newNodes.name: All-volunteer forces
newNodes.emerged: ~1,960 CE end of British National Service call-ups; ~1,973 CE US all-volunteer force
newNodes.prereqRationale: universal_conscription: what it replaces. veterans_benefits: pay and benefits attract volunteers.
newNodes.rationale: universal_conscription: what it replaces. veterans_benefits: pay and benefits attract volunteers.
newNodes.desc: The state ends conscription and recruits paid professionals.
newNodes.effectRationale: Young adults are free to move for work and study.
newNodes.distinctFrom: mercenary_contracts hire foreigners; this recruits citizens as paid volunteers.

newNodes.name: Defence research agencies
newNodes.emerged: ~1,940 CE US National Defense Research Committee; ~1,958 CE ARPA
newNodes.prereqRationale: general_staff: sets requirements. research_university: the labs contracted.
newNodes.rationale: general_staff: sets requirements. research_university: the labs contracted.
newNodes.desc: Defence agencies fund research at universities and laboratories.
newNodes.effectRationale: Defence contracts fund university laboratories.
newNodes.distinctFrom: science_policy funds civil science; this funds military research.

newNodes.name: Independent air force
newNodes.emerged: ~1,918 CE Royal Air Force
newNodes.prereqRationale: general_staff: the command structure. aircraft: the arm.
newNodes.rationale: general_staff: the command structure. aircraft: the arm.
newNodes.desc: Air power is organised as its own service, which flies reconnaissance and survey.
newNodes.effectRationale: Air reconnaissance and survey extend each exploration step.
newNodes.distinctFrom: aircraft is the machine; this is the service.

newNodes.name: Polar research stations
newNodes.emerged: ~1,957 CE International Geophysical Year; ~1,959 CE Antarctic Treaty
newNodes.prereqRationale: international_organizations: the treaty regime. geographical_societies: the exploration tradition.
newNodes.rationale: international_organizations: the treaty regime. geographical_societies: the exploration tradition.
newNodes.desc: States keep permanent scientific stations in the polar regions and share their findings.
newNodes.effectRationale: Permanent stations extend knowledge to the remotest land.
newNodes.distinctFrom: geographical_societies fund expeditions; this keeps permanent shared stations.

newNodes.name: Commonwealth association
newNodes.emerged: ~1,931 CE Statute of Westminster; ~1,949 CE London Declaration
newNodes.prereqRationale: responsible_colonial_government: self-governing dominions. international_organizations: a permanent association.

findings: Dependency changes proposed: 1. settler_land_grants: land_registry AND colonial_administration becomes land_registry AND (colonial_administration OR federal_republic); the Homestead Act anchor was federal, not colonial. Every other edge in the group was assessed and kept.

Leaves bridged by new nodes rather than new edges: trade_treaties (merchant_consuls), state_navy (coaling_stations), mercenary_contracts (colonial_regiments), great_power_congress (river_commissions), settler_land_grants (frontier_development_programmes), decolonization (states_reorganisation, indigenous_land_rights), total_mobilization (wartime_rationing, civil_defence, strategic_stockpiles). Deliberate leaves: dynastic_marriage, daughter_colonies, tributary_relations, military_orders, military_academies, indirect_rule, arms_control, integrated_alliance_command, nuclear_deterrence.

Structural: before this tranche the exploration-empire lane had 6 nodes and no node below A4; new A1-A3 nodes (wayfinding_lore, village_budding, island_voyaging, royal_expeditions, frontier_fortresses) give it a root. The military lane had no logistics strand; campaign_provisioning, military_roads, army_magazines, military_railways and motorized_supply now form one.
No new lane declared: recruitment, command, logistics and doctrine sit in military-institutions; imperial administration and territorial integration sit in exploration-empire.

Operand saturation across all tranche-2 outputs (this group plus the others already written): society.unrestOutputDrag, society.grievanceRelief, trade.gapClosingFraction, trade.costPerBulkCostUnit, research.civicsPointsCoefficient and research.researchPointsCoefficient already exceed their caps in summed deltas. This group adds little to them and leans on under-used operands (governance.authorityDecayCostUnits, roads.*, migration.*, fog.*, colonization.orderPartyFraction, granaries.famineReductionMax, transport.riverCostFactor). Integration should rescale per operand.

fog.exploreMaxRadiusNodes summed across all groups (with this group's 0.26) is about 0.95 of its 1.0 cap; further content should not add to it. fog operands are integers (base step 3, radius 15, sight 1), so small deltas only take effect once accumulated.

Pacing: the existing A8-A9 diplomacy and empire nodes (international_organizations 14,060; collective_security and decolonization 28,130) sit far above their Age medians; with 27 new A9 civics the per-(tree, Age) scale must make A9 nodes cheaper, as section 5 requires.

Chronology note: oath_alliance is A2 but its only era-marked year is ~2,400 BCE (the written attestation), so no Neolithic node can must-hold it. Recommend adding an archaeological date to its emerged text if one is accepted.

integrated_alliance_command rests on collective_security, but NATO is collective defence (UN Charter Art. 51) rather than UN collective security; kept, but a future split into collective_defence may be warranted.
